arguments.summary: Completed-session technical context through the split-adjusted SIP close of 2026-09-18. The five symbols showed broadly positive 21-session relative performance versus SPY except QQQ only modestly, while 63-session leadership was concentrated in ANET and META; MU lagged both benchmarks over 63 sessions despite a positive 21-session rebound. This is descriptive technical evidence only, not an investment conclusion.

claims.text: All return, moving-average, drawdown and realized-volatility observations use 252-session, split-adjusted SIP daily series ending 2026-09-18 and price-return convention. SPY returned -0.96%/2.00% over 21/63 sessions; XLK 3.25%/-0.96%; and XLC -0.46%/1.24%.

ANET recorded 6.94%/17.52% 21/63-session returns, 45.00%/57.14% realized volatility, and a -5.28% drawdown from its 252-session high. Its 21/63-session excess returns were +7.90/+15.51 percentage points versus SPY and +3.69/+18.48 points versus XLK; price was above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs.

QQQ recorded 0.75%/-2.59% 21/63-session returns, 13.19%/20.85% realized volatility, and a -3.31% drawdown from its 252-session high. It exceeded SPY by +1.71/-4.59 percentage points but trailed XLK by -2.50/-1.63 points; price remained above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs.

MU recorded 8.40%/-10.42% 21/63-session returns, 52.49%/89.56% realized volatility, and a -16.30% drawdown from its 252-session high. It exceeded SPY by +9.36/-12.42 percentage points and XLK by +5.15/-9.46 points; price was above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs.

META recorded 21.93%/15.34% 21/63-session returns, 29.31%/44.80% realized volatility, and a -14.67% drawdown from its 252-session high. It exceeded SPY by +22.88/+13.34 percentage points and XLC by +22.38/+14.09 points; price was above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs.

NVDA recorded 2.16%/5.50% 21/63-session returns, 44.72%/39.63% realized volatility, and a -5.71% drawdown from its 252-session high. It exceeded SPY by +3.12/+3.49 percentage points, but trailed XLK by -1.08 points over 21 sessions before exceeding it by +6.46 points over 63; price was above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs.

Conditionally, alignment above the three reported moving averages is consistent with positive completed-session trend structure for all five. Relative leadership is not uniform: META and ANET have positive excess returns at both requested horizons against their sector benchmarks, whereas MU's positive 21-session rebound follows materially negative 63-session relative performance. Realized volatility and drawdown make the strength readings non-equivalent across symbols.

gaps.description: Observations end 2026-09-18 although captured 2026-09-20; they do not cover subsequent sessions. Indicators are simple daily price-series measures, use price returns rather than total returns, and do not establish volume/liquidity, support/resistance, event causality, or forecast probability.
The supplied normalized fields provide a 252-session-window high drawdown, but not the date of that high or a full drawdown path; drawdown duration and recovery cannot be evaluated.

assumptions: Comparisons are valid because the seeded daily series share the 2026-09-18 date, SIP feed, split-adjustment, and price-return convention.
Realized volatility is descriptive historical annualized volatility, not an implied distribution or forward-risk estimate.
arguments.counter_thesis: Moving-average alignment and recent excess returns can reverse; the 63-session MU reversal and QQQ's lag versus XLK illustrate that short-window relative strength is not persistent by itself.

review_conditions.description: At the next data refresh, reassess 21/63-session relative returns, moving-average alignment, and realized volatility using a common completed-session endpoint before relying on this technical context.

question_effects.reason: Macro specialist response was not available in this task; no macro causality is attributed to price behavior.
